To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of chemokine receptors is different in asthmatic ASM cells and that these differences affect chemokine-mediated ASM contraction and migration.
the chemokine receptor CCR2 is expressed by human ASM cells and that CCR2 activation by its ligand MCP-1 induces the migration and proliferation of ASM cells.
CCR2, CCR3, CCR4, CCR7, CXCR1, CXCR2, and CXCR4 are expressed on ASM, and CCL2, CCL3, CCL5, CCL7, CCL11, CXCL1, CXCL5, and CXCL8 are chemokines that induce ASM migration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of chemokines and their receptors on airway smooth muscle function.
the expression of chemokine receptors on ASM cells and the effect of their activation on ASM proliferation and contractile activity.
the role of CCR3 and CCR7 in asthma, with the focus being the ASM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no conclusive evidence for a role of CCR7 in the development and/or progression of asthma.
the expression of chemokine receptors is altered in asthmatic ASM and this is associated with an altered response to chemokines.
the chemokine system is a major player in the pathophysiology of asthma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chemokines are expressed and functional in ASM and may be important in the development of asthma.
chemokine receptors are expressed by ASM and play a role in cell migration.
we have demonstrated a novel role for chemokines in the pathogenesis of asthma, specifically in the regulation of ASM contractility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CCR2 and 5 are expressed by ASM and that CCR2 mediates ASM migration in vitro and in vivo, and that the expression of CCR7 by ASM is regulated by TGF-β.
CCR3, 5, and 7 are all expressed on airway smooth muscle and that CCR3 is the most highly expressed.
chemokine receptors are expressed by human ASM cells and are functionally coupled to intracellular signaling pathways and migration.
